title: Graceful partial toolcall replay and fragment anchoring for SSE multiplexing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Customers report occasional partial tool/function-call outputs after transient client disconnects. Current resume tokens allow continuing from the last chunk boundary but do not provide safe semantics for partially-emitted structured toolcall frames (JSON object open/close split across fragments) when multiplexing multiple logical streams over one SSE connection. This leads to invalid JSON for function call payloads or duplicated side-effects when clients retry naive replays. Goal: define server- and client-side semantics to support graceful partial replay, fragment anchoring, and a compatibility shim for legacy JSONL/eventstream consumers while keeping latency and token-efficiency targets intact.
proposed_solution: Introduce (1) fragment anchors: lightweight 32-bit epoch+offset anchors emitted periodically and attached to SSE chunks so clients can request resume at anchor boundaries; (2) partial-toolcall checkpoints: server marks semantic toolcall boundaries in the stream metadata and emits an immutable checkpoint when a full toolcall payload (structured JSON) has been flushed; (3) idempotent replay hints: server includes an idempotency token for in-flight toolcalls so replays can be ignored by downstream tool adapters; (4) legacy-compatibility mode: when "compatibility=legacy-jsonl" header is present, server emits an extra closing sentinel for open JSONL toolcall frames and a resume-offset mapping shim for older clients. Implementation will be opt-in per-route to avoid extra bandwidth by default.
design_decisions: Emit anchors every ~512 bytes or on semantic boundaries (whichever comes first) to balance resume granularity vs token overhead.
Keep anchors compact (epoch:uint32 + offset:uint32 + rolling-hash:uint64) so they fit in chunk metadata without inflating network frames.
Checkpoints are authoritative: resume at checkpoint replay will not re-execute downstream side-effects. Non-checkpoint resumes may replay idempotent-only parts.
Use idempotency tokens scoped to a single response stream (UUID v4) and include them in tool adapter requests so adapters can dedupe within a TTL window.
Backwards compat: legacy clients get sent a shim layer that closes open structured frames; modern clients ignore the shim via a negotiation header.
Opt-in per-route to avoid cross-customer opt-in regressions; default remains current resume token behavior until rollout completes.
implementation_plan: Proto: extend SSE chunk metadata to include optional 'anchor' and 'checkpoint' fields (runtime wire-level only).
Server: runtime changes to compute anchors during KV-cache flush and annotate emitted chunks (engine team) - PR #1345.
Gateway: update gateway stream multiplexer to respect per-route compatibility header and to synthesize closing sentinels for legacy clients.
Adapters: tool adapter contract extended to accept idempotency_token header for dedupe semantics.
SDKs: JS/Go SDKs add resume helpers to prefer checkpoint resume and expose legacy compatibility flag.
Migrations: feature flag + rollout job for 10% -> 50% -> 100% per-route; monitor trunk.
acceptance_criteria: Client can resume a stream at the last checkpoint and receive a valid, well-formed toolcall JSON payload without duplication of side-effects.
Legacy-compat clients using compatibility header receive a closed sentinel and can recover without manual hacks.
No measurable increase in mean token latency (>2%) for standard workloads when feature flag off; when feature flag on for a route, observed token overhead <=5% in tail scenarios.
Unit/integration tests cover fragment anchors, checkpoint resume, and idempotency dedupe in the tool adapter harness.
Documentation and SDK helpers published (Console docs + quickstart + sample PR to example app).
test_plan: Unit tests: anchor encoding/decoding, epoch rollover edge cases.
Integration: simulate mid-stream disconnects and verify checkpoint vs anchor resume behavior for modern and legacy clients.
Chaos: run fault-injection (packet loss, reorder, duplicate) against multiplexed SSE with concurrent toolcalls.
Load: benchmarks comparing current resume token behavior vs anchor/checkpoint enabled paths across 10k concurrent streams.
Security review: ensure idempotency token does not leak PII and TTL prevents replay attacks (coord with security team).
rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag 'sse-anchor-checkpoint' and enable on internal staging routes for one week.
Stage to 10% of production request traffic for low-risk customer routes; monitor errors, malformed payload rates, and backend side-effect counts.
If stable, expand to 50% and run 72h soak; run additional load tests.
Complete rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and signoff from runtime/console/SDK owners.
